newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Arab Petroleum Investments 1996 net profit rises.
newsitem.headline: Arab Petroleum Investments 1996 net profit rises.

text.p: The Arab Petroleum Investments Corp (APICORP) said on Sunday it posted a net profit of $45 million in 1996, up 12.5 percent from $40 million in 1995.
The board of directors had recommended paying $25 million in dividends to shareholders for 1996, up from $20 million in 1995, a company statement said.
APICORP last year set aside a $5 million provision for assets risk, it added.
Together with regional and international financial institutions it had arranged loans to Arab countries totalling more than $3 billion in 1996.

These included a $1.2 billion deal for Equate Petrochemical Company in Kuwait, a $1.35 billion loan for Qatar's Ras Laffan gas project, a $570 million loan for Qatar Liquefied Gas Co and $110 million for Bahrain's Gulf Petrochemical Industries Co.
It also took part in financing Arab oil exports to Brazil, Pakistan and Germany.
APICORP, based in the eastern Saudi Arabian city of Khobar, is an affiliate of the Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries.
It is owned by Iraq, Libya, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Syria, Qatar, Bahrain, Egypt and Algeria.
APICORP finances oil and petrochemical trade and projects involving Arab states.
